- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.
- csr-transport-bringup: Bring up or audit the hybrid CSR transport for an Andes RISC-V core, given the AndeStar V5 SPA PDF spec and a built vsim engine. Covers the whole pipeline: mine the spec (CSR inventory, IM Requirement / existence conditions, access modes, reset values), classify transport dispositions, bind capability gates to the engine's config.inc, and validate with the reset-hart CSR probe (--probe), the manifest completeness check, --verify, and the e2e suite. Use this skill whenever the user mentions a new core, a new vsim engine, CSR transport / transportation, CSR capability or caps gating, IM Requirement, reset value table, which mode a CSR is supported in, probe-vs-caps mismatches, exec_progbuf cmderr faults, or --verify field mismatches on Andes/M-ext CSRs -- even if they do not say "bring-up" explicitly. Also use it for engine registration work: per-engine test files, CSR manifests, completeness ("nothing missed") checks, or adding a new config of an existing core.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- ralph-loop:cancel-ralph: Cancel active Ralph Loop
- ralph-loop:help: Explain Ralph Loop plugin and available commands
- ralph-loop:ralph-loop: Start Ralph Loop in current session
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Test: QEMU plugin drains vxsat / vxrm / vcsr into the state file.
#
# Runs the probe_v_csr fixture (sets vxrm=1, vxsat=1 before QEMU1 drain)
# and verifies the state binary holds those values at the ABI-locked offsets.
#
# Offsets from state_abi.h / state_abi_check.h (HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX=64):
#   vxsat = 1320 + 32*64 + 0  = 3368
#   vxrm  = 1320 + 32*64 + 8  = 3376
#   vcsr  = 1320 + 32*64 + 16 = 3384
#
# Expected values after the fixture: vxsat=1, vxrm=1, vcsr=3
#   vcsr = (vxrm << 1) | vxsat = (1 << 1) | 1 = 3
#
# Returns 0 (PASS) or 1 (FAIL). Exit code 77 skips when artifacts are absent.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-probe_v_csr}"
hybrid_resolve_paths

SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-probe-vcsr-shared.XXXXXX)
STATE=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE"' EXIT
truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"

# Plugin exits 200 (== kExitHandoffToQemu) on drain; see F1 in ROADMAP.md.
set +e
"$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic \
  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE" 2>/dev/null
rc=$?
set -e
if [[ $rc -ne 200 ]]; then
  echo "FAIL: QEMU expected exit 200 on drain, got rc=$rc"
  exit 1
fi

# Read 8-byte little-endian uint64 at a byte offset from the state file.
read_u64_le() {
  local off=$1
  od -A n -j "$off" -N 8 -t u8 "$STATE" | tr -d ' \n'
}

got_vxsat=$(read_u64_le 3368)
got_vxrm=$(read_u64_le  3376)
got_vcsr=$(read_u64_le  3384)

echo "vxsat=$got_vxsat (want 1)"
echo "vxrm=$got_vxrm  (want 1)"
echo "vcsr=$got_vcsr   (want 3)"

fail=0
[[ "$got_vxsat" == "1" ]] || { echo "FAIL: vxsat=$got_vxsat != 1"; fail=1; }
[[ "$got_vxrm"  == "1" ]] || { echo "FAIL: vxrm=$got_vxrm != 1";  fail=1; }
[[ "$got_vcsr"  == "3" ]] || { echo "FAIL: vcsr=$got_vcsr != 3";   fail=1; }

if [[ $fail -eq 0 ]]; then
  echo "PASS"
  exit 0
else
  exit 1
fi

1	# Out-of-tree build for the QEMU TCG plugin libhybrid_handoff.so. Standalone
2	# from the vsim CMake build because the plugin links against host QEMU's
3	# headers + glib, neither of which exist inside the vsim build container.
4	#
5	# Usage:
6	#   make QEMU_ROOT=/local/nick/qemu_v5
7	#
8	# Output: libhybrid_handoff.so in this directory.
9	
10	QEMU_ROOT ?= /local/nick/qemu_v5
11	CC        ?= gcc
12	
13	GLIB_CFLAGS := $(shell pkg-config --cflags glib-2.0)
14	GLIB_LIBS   := $(shell pkg-config --libs   glib-2.0)
15	
16	CFLAGS  := -O2 -fPIC -Wall -Wextra -std=c11
17	HYBRID_INCLUDE ?= ../include
18	INCLUDES := -I$(HYBRID_INCLUDE) -I$(QEMU_ROOT)/include/qemu $(GLIB_CFLAGS)
19	LDFLAGS := -shared
20	LIBS    := $(GLIB_LIBS)
21	
22	.PHONY: all clean
23	
24	all: libhybrid_handoff.so
25	
26	libhybrid_handoff.so: hybrid_handoff.c bbv_emit.c bbv_emit.h \
27	                     $(HYBRID_INCLUDE)/hybrid/state_abi.h \
28	                     $(HYBRID_INCLUDE)/hybrid/state_abi_check.h \
29	                     $(HYBRID_INCLUDE)/hybrid/insn_match.h
30		@if [ ! -f $(QEMU_ROOT)/include/qemu/qemu-plugin.h ]; then \
31		    echo "error: qemu-plugin.h not under $(QEMU_ROOT)/include/qemu/"; \
32		    echo "       set QEMU_ROOT=<path> on the make command line"; \
33		    exit 1; \
34		fi
35		$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(INCLUDES) $(LDFLAGS) -o $@ hybrid_handoff.c bbv_emit.c $(LIBS)

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# End-to-end harness: QEMU 1 + plugin -> vsim (2-phase, no QEMU2 handback).
3	#
4	# Memory between QEMU and vsim is shared via an /dev/shm-backed mmap
5	# (128 MB). Works for both asm fixtures (handoff_roundtrip, rt_*) and
6	# C-level fixtures (rt_c_*). C fixtures require shared mmap so the
7	# stack/heap survives the handoff; asm fixtures don't need it but run
8	# fine with it.
9	#
10	# Env:
11	#   FIXTURE         REQUIRED. .elf name under tests/fixtures/ (no .elf suffix).
12	#   TRIGGER_MODE    csr | pc (default csr).
13	#   TIMEOUT         vsim leg timeout in seconds (default 60).
14	#   CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC=1   assert mcycle/minstret strictly increased
15	#                              between QEMU 1's drain and vsim's drain.
16	#   VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN, VSIM_ELF, NM  override built paths.
17	
18	set -euo pipefail
19	
20	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
21	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/paths.sh"
22	
23	FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:?FIXTURE env var is required (e.g. FIXTURE=rt_c_hello)}"
24	TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-60}"
25	TRIGGER_MODE="${TRIGGER_MODE:-csr}"
26	
27	hybrid_resolve_paths
28	
29	NM="${NM:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}}"
30	NM="${NM:-riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}"
31	
32	case "$TRIGGER_MODE" in
33	  csr) ;;
34	  pc)
35	    if ! command -v "$NM" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
36	      echo "skip[$FIXTURE pc]: nm not found at $NM"
37	      exit 77
38	    fi
39	    NM_OUT=$("$NM" --defined-only "$VSIM_ELF")
40	    ENTER_PC=$(printf '%s\n' "$NM_OUT" | awk '$3=="_hybrid_enter_pc"{print $1}')
41	    EXIT_PC=$(printf '%s\n' "$NM_OUT"  | awk '$3=="_hybrid_exit_pc"{print $1}')
42	    if [ -z "${ENTER_PC:-}" ] || [ -z "${EXIT_PC:-}" ]; then
43	      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE pc]: missing _hybrid_enter_pc/_hybrid_exit_pc symbols"
44	      exit 1
45	    fi
46	    ;;
47	  *)
48	    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: unknown TRIGGER_MODE=$TRIGGER_MODE (use csr|pc)"
49	    exit 1
50	    ;;
51	esac
52	
53	# 128 MB matches the QEMU virt machine default; vsim uses the same size.
54	SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
55	SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-e2e-shared.XXXXXX)
56	STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
57	STATE_VSIM=$(mktemp)
58	SIM_LOG=$(mktemp)
59	trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$STATE_VSIM" "$SIM_LOG"' EXIT
60	truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"
61	
62	PLUGIN_ARGS="outfile=$STATE_QEMU"
63	VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=()
64	if [ "$TRIGGER_MODE" = "pc" ]; then
65	  PLUGIN_ARGS="$PLUGIN_ARGS,enter_pc=0x$ENTER_PC"
66	  VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=(--hybrid-exit-pc "0x$EXIT_PC")
67	fi
68	
69	echo "[$FIXTURE 1/2 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] QEMU 1: drain entry state"
70	set +e
71	"$VSIM_QEMU" \
72	  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
73	  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
74	  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
75	  -nographic \
76	  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
77	  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
78	  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,$PLUGIN_ARGS" >/dev/null 2>&1
79	QEMU1_RC=$?
80	set -e
81	
82	if [ "$QEMU1_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
83	  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 expected exit 200 on drain, got $QEMU1_RC"
84	  exit 1
85	fi
86	
87	if [ ! -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
88	  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 did not produce state"
89	  exit 1
90	fi
91	
92	echo "[$FIXTURE 2/2 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] vsim: resume + drain"
93	set +e
94	timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_ELF" \
95	  --resume-from-qemu "$STATE_QEMU" \
96	  --handoff-out "$STATE_VSIM" \
97	  --shared-mem-path "$SHARED_MEM" \
98	  --shared-mem-size "$SHARED_SIZE" \
99	  --shared-mem-base 0x00000000 \
100	  "${VSIM_TRIG_ARGS[@]}" >"$SIM_LOG" 2>&1
101	VSIM_RC=$?
102	set -e
103	
104	# Opt-in: mcycle/minstret must strictly increase from QEMU 1's drain
105	# to vsim's drain. Offsets locked by state_abi_check.h (mcycle@624,
106	# minstret@632). Runs before the RC gate so the verdict is independent
107	# of any downstream failure.
108	if [ "${CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC:-0}" = "1" ] && [ -s "$STATE_VSIM" ]; then
109	  read_u64_le() { od -A n -j "$1" -N 8 -t u8 "$2" | tr -d ' \n'; }
110	  Q1_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le 624 "$STATE_QEMU")
111	  Q1_MINST=$(read_u64_le  632 "$STATE_QEMU")
112	  V_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le  624 "$STATE_VSIM")
113	  V_MINST=$(read_u64_le   632 "$STATE_VSIM")
114	  echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] qemu1: mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE minstret=$Q1_MINST"
115	  echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] vsim:  mcycle=$V_MCYCLE minstret=$V_MINST"
116	  if [ "$V_MCYCLE" -le "$Q1_MCYCLE" ]; then
117	    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: mcycle not strictly increasing across vsim"
118	    exit 1
119	  fi
120	  if [ "$V_MINST" -le "$Q1_MINST" ]; then
121	    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: minstret not strictly increasing across vsim"
122	    exit 1
123	  fi
124	  echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] PASS: strictly increasing"
125	fi
126	
127	# vsim drained on the exit trigger and exited 200 (kExitHandoffToQemu).
128	# Anything else is a hard failure: the run is only complete when vsim
129	# drained cleanly.
130	if [ "$VSIM_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
131	  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: vsim expected exit 200 (drain), got $VSIM_RC"
132	  echo "--- sim log ---"
133	  cat "$SIM_LOG"
134	  exit 1
135	fi
136	
137	if [ ! -s "$STATE_VSIM" ]; then
138	  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: vsim did not produce a drained state file"
139	  exit 1
140	fi
141	
142	echo "[$FIXTURE PASS] 2-phase handoff complete (QEMU 1 drain -> vsim drain)"
143

1	# Build tiny RV64 fixtures used by hybrid smoke tests.
2	#
3	# Toolchain location comes from the repo-root config.env (loaded by
4	# `source ./setup.sh`, which exports HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). Override on the
5	# command line with `make TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain ...` if you want
6	# to bypass the env var.
7	
8	TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
9	ifeq ($(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),)
10	$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass `TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain` on the command line)
11	endif
12	CC        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
13	LD        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ld
14	OBJDUMP   := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump
15	
16	CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
17	LDFLAGS := -T test.ld -nostdlib -static
18	
19	# All fixtures share test.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
20	RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
21	               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
22	               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival
23	
24	# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
25	# against the Andes virtual-hosting libgloss (libgloss_vh.a), which
26	# implements _write / _exit / _sbrk / _read / ... via the RISC-V
27	# semihosting magic triple. QEMU1 is launched with
28	# -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native and intercepts the triple
29	# before it reaches mtvec. vsim does not implement semihosting -- phase
30	# 2 (the span between enter_vsim and exit_vsim)
31	# is therefore syscall-free by rule (see runtime/rt_c_helpers.h).
32	RT_C_FIXTURES    := rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_static_buf \
33	                    rt_c_no_trigger_exit
34	RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul
35	# Probe fixtures: QEMU1-only, no vsim phase. Used by shell tests
36	# that inspect the raw state file to verify plugin drain behavior.
37	PROBE_V_FIXTURES := probe_v_csr
38	
39	RUNTIME_DIR     := runtime
40	RUNTIME_SRCS    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/crt0.S $(RUNTIME_DIR)/trap.S \
41	                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/handler.c
42	# V fixtures use the standard C runtime (RUNTIME_SRCS). V regfile transport
43	# is handled transparently inside vsim via the Debug Module Program Buffer
44	# (ResumeDriver/StateDrain), so no per-fixture transport TU is linked.
45	# -nodefaultlibs suppresses the toolchain's default -lc/-lgloss/-lgcc;
46	# we re-add them inside --start-group so -lgloss_vh's semihosting stubs
47	# resolve newlib's _write / _exit / _sbrk / ... before -lgloss (the
48	# proxy-kernel ecall variant) is even searched. Order matters:
49	# -lgloss_vh must precede the fallback -lgloss path.
50	RT_C_LIBS       := -Wl,--start-group -lc -lgloss_vh -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
51	RT_C_CFLAGS     := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -static -nostartfiles \
52	                   -nodefaultlibs -I$(RUNTIME_DIR) -Wall
53	# RVV-using fixtures need -march=rv64gcv. The crt0 already sets
54	# mstatus.VS to Initial, so V instructions don't trap.
55	RT_C_V_CFLAGS   := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -static -nostartfiles \
56	                   -nodefaultlibs -I$(RUNTIME_DIR) -Wall
57	
58	.PHONY: all clean dump demo
59	
60	all: spin.elf icount_spin.elf handoff.elf handoff_exit.elf handoff_roundtrip.elf \
61	     $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
62	     $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
63	     $(PROBE_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)
64	
65	# Note: handoff.elf, handoff_exit.elf, spin.elf are legacy (referenced only
66	# by EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL handoff_smoke.cpp). They still build for completeness
67	# but are not in active CTest. All targets now share test.ld at 0x00100000.
68	
69	# Switching-mode demo runner: builds the fixtures if needed, then walks
70	# T1..T7 from $(DEMO_DIR), printing a banner per mode and a final
71	# pass/fail tally. Honors FILTER=<regex> to subset the run.
72	demo: all
73		@bash demo.sh
74	
75	spin.elf: spin.S test.ld
76		$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c spin.S -o spin.o
77		$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) spin.o -o $@
78	
79	# CSR-less spin for F5 plugin-icount e2e. Linked at 0x00100000 (test.ld)
80	# so andes_ae350's MROM at 0x80000000 stays clear when loaded via -bios.
81	icount_spin.elf: icount_spin.S test.ld
82		$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c icount_spin.S -o icount_spin.o
83		$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) icount_spin.o -o $@
84	
85	handoff.elf: handoff.S test.ld
86		$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff.S -o handoff.o
87		$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff.o -o $@
88	
89	handoff_exit.elf: handoff_exit.S test.ld
90		$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_exit.S -o handoff_exit.o
91		$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_exit.o -o $@
92	
93	handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S test.ld semihost_exit.inc
94		$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
95		$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@
96	
97	$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S test.ld semihost_exit.inc
98		$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
99		$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@
100	
101	# C-level fixtures: compile+link via gcc (newlib pulled). crt0.S is
102	# passed FIRST so _start lands at the load address (0x00100000) -- ld
103	# preserves input order within the .text wildcard.
104	$(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(RUNTIME_SRCS) test.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
105		$(CC) $(RT_C_CFLAGS) -T test.ld \
106		  $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $< $(RT_C_LIBS) -o $@
107	
108	# RVV-enabled fixtures: same runtime as the C fixtures, different -march.
109	# Listed separately so changes to RT_C_CFLAGS don't accidentally drop V.
110	$(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(RUNTIME_SRCS) test.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
111		$(CC) $(RT_C_V_CFLAGS) -T test.ld \
112		  $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $< $(RT_C_LIBS) -o $@
113	
114	# Probe fixtures: pure asm, -march=rv64gcv (need V CSR names), no C runtime.
115	PROBE_V_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
116	$(PROBE_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S test.ld
117		$(CC) $(PROBE_V_CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
118		$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@
119	
120	dump: spin.elf handoff.elf handoff_exit.elf
121		$(OBJDUMP) -d spin.elf
122		$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff.elf
123		$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff_exit.elf
124	
125	clean:
126		rm -f spin.o spin.elf handoff.o handoff.elf handoff_exit.o handoff_exit.elf \
127		      handoff_roundtrip.o handoff_roundtrip.elf \
128		      $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
129		      $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
130		      $(PROBE_V_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(PROBE_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)
131

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Run the hybrid e2e tests directly, bypassing the VSIM_ENABLE_HYBRID
3	# CTest gate. Drives tests/*.sh against pre-built artifacts in this
4	# workspace.
5	#
6	# Env overrides:
7	#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64 (default: build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64)
8	#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so (default: qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so)
9	#   VSIM_BIN     sim_<cpu> (default: first sim_* under verilator/build/)
10	#   FILTER       regex; only run tests whose name matches
11	#   MODE         csr | pc | both  (default: both) - drives TRIGGER_MODE
12	#                for round-trip fixtures. Negative drivers run once
13	#                regardless because they assert harness failure
14	#                modes orthogonal to the trigger mechanism.
15	#   JOBS         parallel job slots (default: min($(nproc),
16	#                free(/dev/shm)/256MB)). Each Tier-2 slot uses a 128 MB
17	#                /dev/shm mmap and runs 2 processes (qemu1, vsim); the
18	#                headroom check leaves margin for that plus QEMU's own
19	#                scratch. Pass JOBS=1 for sequential semantics.
20	#   LOG_DIR      where per-test logs land (default: mktemp -d under /tmp)
21	
22	set -euo pipefail
23	
24	ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
25	VSIM_DIR="$ROOT/verilator"
26	HARNESS="$ROOT/tests"
27	TEST_DIR="$ROOT/tests/fixtures"
28	
29	VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64}"
30	VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"
31	if [[ -z "${VSIM_BIN:-}" ]]; then
32	  VSIM_BIN=$(ls "$VSIM_DIR"/build/sim_* 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)
33	fi
34	
35	step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
36	ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
37	warn() { printf '\033[1;33m[skip]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
38	fail() { printf '\033[1;31m[FAIL]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
39	
40	require() {
41	  if [[ -z "$2" || ! -e "$2" ]]; then
42	    fail "$1 not found: $2"
43	    fail "build artifacts first: 'source ./setup.sh'"
44	    exit 1
45	  fi
46	}
47	require VSIM_QEMU   "$VSIM_QEMU"
48	require VSIM_PLUGIN "$VSIM_PLUGIN"
49	require VSIM_BIN    "$VSIM_BIN"
50	
51	export VSIM_QEMU VSIM_PLUGIN VSIM_BIN
52	
53	REQUIRED_ELFS=(
54	  handoff_roundtrip rt_pc_jump rt_sign_bits rt_abi_aliases rt_long_roi
55	  rt_all_gprs rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh rt_csr_survival rt_shared_mem
56	  rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs
57	  rt_c_v_matmul
58	  # icount_spin: CSR-less spin loop. Used by switching-mode demos
59	  # T3/T4/T5 (icount, BBV emit, slice-consume).
60	  icount_spin
61	)
62	need_build=0
63	for f in "${REQUIRED_ELFS[@]}"; do
64	  [[ -e "$TEST_DIR/$f.elf" ]] || need_build=1
65	done
66	if (( need_build )); then
67	  step "building test ELFs in $TEST_DIR"
68	  make -C "$TEST_DIR" -j
69	fi
70	
71	# Round-trip fixtures: name|fixture-env-prefix. All run on the unified
72	# e2e.sh harness (shared /dev/shm mmap). The TRIGGER_MODE env is
73	# injected per iteration based on $MODE. Negative drivers live in
74	# NEG_TESTS and run once regardless of mode.
75	RT_TESTS=(
76	  "handoff_roundtrip|FIXTURE=handoff_roundtrip"
77	  "rt_pc_jump|FIXTURE=rt_pc_jump"
78	  "rt_sign_bits|FIXTURE=rt_sign_bits"
79	  "rt_abi_aliases|FIXTURE=rt_abi_aliases"
80	  "rt_long_roi|FIXTURE=rt_long_roi"
81	  "rt_all_gprs|FIXTURE=rt_all_gprs"
82	  "rt_mem_loadstore|FIXTURE=rt_mem_loadstore"
83	  "rt_unaligned_lh|FIXTURE=rt_unaligned_lh"
84	  "rt_csr_survival|FIXTURE=rt_csr_survival"
85	  "rt_shared_mem|FIXTURE=rt_shared_mem"
86	  "rt_c_hello|FIXTURE=rt_c_hello"
87	  "rt_c_printf|FIXTURE=rt_c_printf"
88	  "rt_c_matmul|FIXTURE=rt_c_matmul TIMEOUT=120"
89	  "rt_c_v_regs|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_regs"
90	  "rt_c_v_csrs|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_csrs"
91	  "rt_c_v_matmul|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_matmul TIMEOUT=120"
92	  "rt_c_static_buf|FIXTURE=rt_c_static_buf"
93	)
94	
95	NEG_TESTS=(
96	  "rt_corrupt_state|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_corrupt_state.sh"
97	)
98	
99	# Switching-mode demos (T1-T5, one per trigger pathway). Each demo
100	# exercises one trigger pathway end-to-end. Run once (no
101	# csr/pc/both loop) because each script hard-codes its trigger choice.
102	DEMO_TESTS=(
103	  "demo_csr_oneshot|bash $HARNESS/demos/demo_csr_oneshot.sh"
104	  "demo_pc_oneshot|bash $HARNESS/demos/demo_pc_oneshot.sh"
105	  "demo_icount_roundtrip|bash $HARNESS/demos/demo_icount_roundtrip.sh"
106	  "demo_bbv_profile|bash $HARNESS/demos/demo_bbv_profile.sh"
107	  "demo_slice_consume_roundtrip|bash $HARNESS/demos/demo_slice_consume_roundtrip.sh"
108	)
109	
110	MODE="${MODE:-both}"
111	case "$MODE" in
112	  csr|pc|both) ;;
113	  *) fail "MODE must be one of csr|pc|both (got: $MODE)"; exit 1 ;;
114	esac
115	
116	default_jobs() {
117	  local n=1 shm_free shm_cap
118	  n=$(nproc 2>/dev/null || echo 1)
119	  if [[ -d /dev/shm ]]; then
120	    shm_free=$(df -m --output=avail /dev/shm 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | tr -d ' ')
121	    if [[ "$shm_free" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$shm_free" -gt 0 ]]; then
122	      shm_cap=$((shm_free / 256))
123	      (( shm_cap < n && shm_cap >= 1 )) && n=$shm_cap
124	    fi
125	  fi
126	  (( n < 1 )) && n=1
127	  printf '%d\n' "$n"
128	}
129	JOBS="${JOBS:-$(default_jobs)}"
130	[[ "$JOBS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$JOBS" -ge 1 ]] \
131	  || { fail "JOBS must be a positive integer (got: $JOBS)"; exit 1; }
132	
133	FILTER="${FILTER:-}"
134	
135	LOG_DIR="${LOG_DIR:-$(mktemp -d -t e2e-XXXXXX)}"
136	mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
137	RESULTS_FILE="$LOG_DIR/results.tsv"
138	LOCK_FILE="$LOG_DIR/lock"
139	: > "$RESULTS_FILE"
140	: > "$LOCK_FILE"
141	
142	# run_one MODE NAME CMD INDEX TOTAL
143	# Captures the test command's stdout+stderr into $LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log,
144	# emits one atomic progress line, and appends a TSV row to $RESULTS_FILE
145	# (mode<TAB>name<TAB>status<TAB>rc<TAB>elapsed). flock on $LOCK_FILE
146	# serializes the progress write and the results-file append so concurrent
147	# children (introduced by the parallel-execution commit) cannot interleave
148	# their TTY writes or corrupt the tally file.
149	run_one() {
150	  local mode="$1" name="$2" cmd="$3" idx="$4" total="$5"
151	  local log="$LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log"
152	  local start end elapsed status rc
153	  start=$(date +%s)
154	  set +e
155	  bash -c "$cmd" >"$log" 2>&1
156	  rc=$?
157	  set -e
158	  end=$(date +%s)
159	  elapsed=$((end - start))
160	  case $rc in
161	    0)  status=PASS ;;
162	    77) status=SKIP ;;
163	    *)  status=FAIL ;;
164	  esac
165	  (
166	    flock 9
167	    case "$status" in
168	      PASS) ok   "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (${elapsed}s)" ;;
169	      SKIP) warn "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=77, ${elapsed}s)" ;;
170	      FAIL) fail "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=$rc, ${elapsed}s) -> $log" ;;
171	    esac
172	    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%d\t%d\n' \
173	      "$mode" "$name" "$status" "$rc" "$elapsed" >> "$RESULTS_FILE"
174	  ) 9>"$LOCK_FILE"
175	}
176	
177	# Build the workplan: one entry per (mode, name, cmd) tuple. Order
178	# matters: csr-mode tests first, then pc-mode, then negatives (matching
179	# the original sequential layout so logs are streamed in the same order).
180	declare -a WORKPLAN=()
181	for tm in csr pc; do
182	  [[ "$MODE" != "both" && "$MODE" != "$tm" ]] && continue
183	  for entry in "${RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
184	    rt_name="${entry%%|*}"
185	    env_prefix="${entry#*|}"
186	    [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$rt_name" =~ $FILTER ]] && continue
187	    cmd="TRIGGER_MODE=$tm $env_prefix bash $HARNESS/e2e.sh"
188	    WORKPLAN+=("$tm|$rt_name|$cmd")
189	  done
190	done
191	for entry in "${NEG_TESTS[@]}"; do
192	  neg_name="${entry%%|*}"
193	  neg_cmd="${entry#*|}"
194	  [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$neg_name" =~ $FILTER ]] && continue
195	  WORKPLAN+=("neg|$neg_name|$neg_cmd")
196	done
197	for entry in "${DEMO_TESTS[@]}"; do
198	  demo_name="${entry%%|*}"
199	  demo_cmd="${entry#*|}"
200	  [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$demo_name" =~ $FILTER ]] && continue
201	  WORKPLAN+=("demo|$demo_name|$demo_cmd")
202	done
203	
204	TOTAL=${#WORKPLAN[@]}
205	step "logs: $LOG_DIR  jobs: $JOBS  mode: $MODE  tests: $TOTAL"
206	
207	# FIFO-based bounded job pool. Each child reads one token from $SEM_FIFO
208	# before starting and writes one back on exit; only $JOBS tokens exist,
209	# so at most $JOBS children run concurrently. Opening the fifo in
210	# read-write mode (<>) means writes never block the parent. The fifo
211	# inode is unlinked immediately after fd 8 is bound -- the kernel keeps
212	# the pipe alive as long as fd 8 is open.
213	SEM_FIFO="$LOG_DIR/sem.fifo"
214	mkfifo "$SEM_FIFO"
215	exec 8<>"$SEM_FIFO"
216	rm -f "$SEM_FIFO"
217	for ((sem_i=0; sem_i<JOBS; sem_i++)); do
218	  printf '.\n' >&8
219	done
220	
221	i=0
222	for w in "${WORKPLAN[@]}"; do
223	  i=$((i+1))
224	  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
225	  w_rest="${w#*|}"
226	  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
227	  w_cmd="${w_rest#*|}"
228	  read -r -u 8 _tok
229	  (
230	    run_one "$w_mode" "$w_name" "$w_cmd" "$i" "$TOTAL"
231	    printf '.\n' >&8
232	  ) &
233	done
234	wait
235	exec 8>&-
236	
237	declare -A MODE_PASS=([csr]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0 [demo]=0)
238	declare -A MODE_FAIL=([csr]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0 [demo]=0)
239	declare -A MODE_SKIP=([csr]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0 [demo]=0)
240	declare -a FAILED_NAMES=()
241	while IFS=$'\t' read -r r_mode r_name r_status _r_rc _r_el; do
242	  case "$r_status" in
243	    PASS) MODE_PASS[$r_mode]=$((MODE_PASS[$r_mode]+1)) ;;
244	    SKIP) MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]=$((MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]+1)) ;;
245	    FAIL) MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]=$((MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]+1));
246	          FAILED_NAMES+=("${r_name}[${r_mode}]") ;;
247	  esac
248	done < "$RESULTS_FILE"
249	
250	# Stream failed-test logs in workplan order so the user sees a
251	# deterministic post-run failure dump.
252	for w in "${WORKPLAN[@]}"; do
253	  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
254	  w_rest="${w#*|}"
255	  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
256	  w_status=$(awk -F'\t' -v m="$w_mode" -v n="$w_name" \
257	                 '$1==m&&$2==n{print $3; exit}' "$RESULTS_FILE")
258	  if [[ "$w_status" == "FAIL" ]]; then
259	    echo
260	    echo "=== FAIL log: ${w_name}[${w_mode}] ==="
261	    cat "$LOG_DIR/$w_mode--$w_name.log"
262	  fi
263	done
264	
265	echo
266	csr_p=${MODE_PASS[csr]} csr_f=${MODE_FAIL[csr]} csr_s=${MODE_SKIP[csr]}
267	pc_p=${MODE_PASS[pc]}   pc_f=${MODE_FAIL[pc]}   pc_s=${MODE_SKIP[pc]}
268	neg_p=${MODE_PASS[neg]} neg_f=${MODE_FAIL[neg]} neg_s=${MODE_SKIP[neg]}
269	dem_p=${MODE_PASS[demo]} dem_f=${MODE_FAIL[demo]} dem_s=${MODE_SKIP[demo]}
270	total_pass=$((csr_p + pc_p + neg_p + dem_p))
271	total_fail=$((csr_f + pc_f + neg_f + dem_f))
272	total_skip=$((csr_s + pc_s + neg_s + dem_s))
273	step "summary: csr ${csr_p}p/${csr_f}f/${csr_s}s  pc ${pc_p}p/${pc_f}f/${pc_s}s  neg ${neg_p}p/${neg_f}f/${neg_s}s  demo ${dem_p}p/${dem_f}f/${dem_s}s  total ${total_pass} passed, ${total_fail} failed, ${total_skip} skipped"
274	if (( total_fail > 0 )); then
275	  fail "failures: ${FAILED_NAMES[*]}"
276	  exit 1
277	fi

    Remove icount trigger, simpoint-driven trigger, and cosim features
    
    Removes three feature families end to end (code, build, tests, docs):

      tools/simpoint submodule.

      and cycle lock-step DV (--mode cycle --cosim, --cosim-lockstep), the
      driver cosim_lockstep core, the plugin cosim_*/lockstep_* oracle modes,
      and cosim_redesign.md / the cosim tutorial notebook.
    
    Also removes the gem5-style warmup window (--vsim-warmup-icount, the
    mcycle/minstret_at_measure_start wire-ABI fields, and the orchestrator
    warmup/measure/total breakdown), which was specific to these paths.
    
    Survives: --mode fast|cycle|hybrid, the marker/pc triggers, --verify, the
    hybrid handoff, state drain/resume, and archive/replay. Bumps the verilator
    submodule to the matching hybrid-layer removal.

1	# hybrid_sim
2	
3	Workspace for the Andes hybrid simulator: QEMU 9.x (functional, MHz) + vsim
4	(SystemC + Verilator, cycle-accurate) sharing memory and architectural state
5	across a magic-CSR boundary.
6	
7	Two submodules:
8	
9	- `QEMU/` - QEMU fork hosting the TCG plugin
10	- `verilator/` - vsim sources, including `hybrid/qemu_plugin/` (plugin source)
11	
12	## Quickstart
13	
14	```sh
15	git clone --recursive https://gitea.andestech.com/nick/hybrid_sim && cd hybrid_sim
16	source ./setup.sh                # build qemu, vsim, plugin, simpoint
17	make -C tests/fixtures -j        # build the RISC-V ELF fixtures
18	bash scripts/run_e2e.sh          # full e2e suite
19	```
20	
21	See `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` Sections 1-5 for the developer-grade scripts
22	(`setup.sh`, `tests/e2e.sh`, `scripts/run_e2e.sh`).
23	
24	## Host dependencies
25	
26	- C/C++ toolchain (clang preferred), CMake >= 3.20, ninja
27	- Python 3
28	- glib-2.0 dev (for the QEMU plugin)
29	- pkg-config
30	- Verilator (auto-detected; set `VSIM_VERILATOR_EXECUTABLE` if needed)
31	- libraries QEMU itself needs (pixman, slirp, etc. - see `QEMU/README.rst`)
32	
33	## Outputs
34	
35	After `./build.sh`:
36	
37	- `QEMU/build/qemu-system-riscv64`
38	- `verilator/build/vsim`
39	- `verilator/hybrid/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so`

# ROADMAP: Andes HybridSim v1.0 (complete-all-features)

Single source of truth for everything required to ship Andes HybridSim
v1.0. Every feature traces to a functional requirement in `docs/FRS.md`,
which in turn traces to a market requirement in `docs/MRD.md`. Covering
all FRs therefore covers all MRs (FRS section 13 has no orphan).

This file **supersedes** two earlier engineering breakdowns, now in
`docs/archive/`:

- `docs/archive/commercial_v1_roadmap.md` - Waves 0-6 closing L1-L21
- `docs/archive/TODO.md` - failure-mode backlog F-T1.1..F-T3.8

Their content is absorbed below as full feature entries. `docs/andes_sim_limitations.ipynb`
stays as the plain-English "do not do this" envelope and the L-id source.

House rules (from `CLAUDE.md`): one session completes one feature. Update
the feature's Status when starting (in-progress) and on completion (done).
Each code feature carries a TDD RED line: the failing test you write first.

## Status legend

- not-started: no work yet
- in-progress: being implemented in a session
- partial: shipped for the M-mode envelope, incomplete for the full FR
- done: behavioural + structural commits landed, tests pass
- business: not a code task; a sign-off / process / legal deliverable

## Feature ID scheme

- `F-ENG-*` - engineering: ROI-envelope and correctness of the cycle engine
- `F-PROD-*` - productization: interfaces, trace, observability, encryption,
  licensing, packaging
- `F-BIZ-*` - business / legal / process: tagged `business`, no TDD RED

# Build tiny RV64 fixtures used by hybrid smoke tests.
#
# Toolchain location comes from the repo-root config.env (loaded by
# `source ./setup.sh`, which exports HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). Override on the
# command line with `make TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain ...` if you want
# to bypass the env var.

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
# rv64 tools. The toolchain check is deferred to use-time (recursive `=` +
# $(error)), so a pure-rv32 `make rv32` -- which uses CC32/LD32 below -- needs
# only HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32, not HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN.
rv64_tc   = $(if $(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),$(TOOLCHAIN),$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain))
CC        = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
LD        = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ld
OBJDUMP   = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump

# Runtime sources live at the repo root (runtime/) -- they are the
# user-facing andesim runtime; fixtures are just one consumer. The linker
# script moved with them (test.ld -> runtime/andesim.ld, same content).
RUNTIME_DIR := ../../runtime
LDSCRIPT    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld
# Fixture-only helpers (csr ROI markers; NOT part of the portable runtime).
HELPERS_DIR := runtime

CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
LDFLAGS := -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static

# All fixtures share andesim.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_all_fprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival rt_m_ext_counters \
               rt_m_ext_trigcause rt_priv_smode rt_priv_umode

# Attack / breakage programs: each demonstrates a bug in the hybrid handoff.
# NOT part of the standard 'all' target (they are expected to misbehave).
# Build individually: make break_vscratch.elf   (etc.)
BREAK_FIXTURES := break_vscratch break_vscratch_top break_mcycle_write \
                  break_verify_diverge

# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
# through the shipped vplat runtime (libandesim_runtime.a) with the
# same two-flag command users type (-B build/runtime
# -specs=andesim.specs), so the suites regression-test the real
# artifact. stdio goes out the ATCUART100 UART2 and exit/file-io through
# the SimControl device at 0xe0080000, all of which both QEMU's
# andes_ae350 and vsim model. No semihosting and no libgloss anywhere:
# vplat_syscalls.o in the archive provides every stub newlib needs, so
# the same ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid and a syscall inside the
# ROI works (it just adds its real cycles to the figure).
RT_C_FIXTURES    := rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_static_buf \
                    rt_c_fcsr
RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul rt_c_v_fill
RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_hello vplat_exit41 vplat_file

RUNTIME_SRCS    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/crt0.S $(RUNTIME_DIR)/trap.S \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/handler.c
# Prereqs of the runtime grouped target(s) -- shared by the rv64 and rv32 rules.
RUNTIME_DEPS    := $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(RUNTIME_DIR)/vplat_syscalls.c \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/ROI.h
VPLAT_RT_DIR := ../../build/runtime
VPLAT_RT     := $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/crt0.o \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h
VPLAT_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall
# RVV-using fixtures need -march=rv64gcv; the runtime's rv64gc objects
# link cleanly into rv64gcv programs (ld unions the arch attributes).
# The crt0 already sets mstatus.VS to Initial, so V insns don't trap.
VPLAT_V_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall

# --- rv32 fixtures (docs/rv32_ROADMAP.md F3) ---------------------------------
# A small rv32 set for the arch-match path; the bulk of the fixtures stay rv64.
# Built via `make rv32` (NOT part of `all`), only when HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 is set.
# rv32_c_hello reuses rt_c_hello.c (markers are arch-neutral HINTs); rv32_spin
# reuses spin.S. The rv32 runtime comes from build/runtime/rv32 (ARCH=rv32).
TOOLCHAIN32    ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32)
CC32           := $(TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc
LD32           := $(TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-ld
CFLAGS32       := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -nostdlib -static -Wall
VPLAT_CFLAGS32 := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -O1 -Wall

# Switching-Mode Tutorial and Exercises

Status: draft for review
Audience: engineer running the hybrid simulator for the first time
Scope: the 2 switching modes the repo ships, with copy-paste commands,
the cycle figure each one yields, and one exercise per mode.

---

## 0. What "switching mode" means

The hybrid simulator runs a program across two phases:

```
   QEMU1  --(state file + shared mmap)-->  vsim
   (fast)                                 (cycle accurate)
```

A "switching mode" is the RULE that decides WHEN QEMU1 drains its
architectural state and hands the region of interest to vsim. vsim runs
that region cycle-accurately, then drains the final state. You pick
the rule with plugin args and vsim CLI flags; the fixture binary does not
have to change between modes.

> **Two ways to invoke, one canonical.** `./andesim run` is the driver -
> the supported way to run a workload, and what the examples below lead
> with. `tests/e2e.sh` is the regression harness that wraps the same legs
> behind `FIXTURE=... TRIGGER_MODE=... bash tests/e2e.sh`; it adds test-only
> assertions (`CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC`, `EXPECT_RC`, ...) and is shown only
> where those diagnostics are the point. When in doubt, use `./andesim run`.

The repo ships **2 modes**, both profiling a kernel.

### Quick map

| # | Mode | Profiles | Switch boundary | Cycle figure it yields |
|---|------|----------|-----------------|------------------------|
| 1 | marker | a kernel | `slti x0,x0,0x5A0` (enter) / `slti x0,x0,0x5A1` (exit) | kernel cycles |
| 2 | PC | a kernel | a PC / symbol address (no source edit) | kernel cycles |

- **Kernel modes (marker, PC)** measure ONE region you choose.

(Migration: the old M1-M8 list collapses to these 2. Old M8 - the QEMU2
semihosting exit - was removed with the QEMU2 phase, so every run now ends
at the vsim drain.)

### Where the cycle figure comes from

Every mode reads the same counter: `mcycle`, a little-endian `uint64` at
byte offset **624** in the state file (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`). vsim

1	# Hybrid Simulator User Guide
2	
3	Audience: a new engineer who wants to RUN the Andes hybrid simulator,
4	not study its internals. After this guide you can:
5	
6	1. Build every artifact from a fresh clone.
7	2. Configure QEMU, vsim, and the harness for a workload.
8	3. Pick a switching mode (M1..M5) and run one handoff end-to-end
9	   with a concrete worked example.
10	
11	For internals, read `docs/HYBRID_OVERVIEW.md`. For per-mode drill-down,
12	read `docs/switching_modes_tutorial.md`.
13	
14	---
15	
16	## 0. The one-paragraph mental model
17	
18	QEMU runs the boring parts at MHz. vsim (Verilator + SystemC) runs the
19	small region-of-interest at cycle accuracy. They share RAM via an
20	`mmap` file. A magic trigger (CSR write, PC, or instruction count)
21	hands control between them. One run is two legs:
22	
23	```
24	   QEMU1  -- state.bin + shared mmap -->  vsim
25	   (fast)                                 (cycle accurate; run ends here)
26	```
27	
28	The run ends at vsim's exit-trigger drain (there is no QEMU2 leg). The
29	thing you choose per run is the TRIGGER that decides where each leg
30	drains and the next leg resumes. That choice is the "switching mode".
31	
32	---
33	
34	## 1. Build and environment setup
35	
36	### 1.1 Host prerequisites
37	
38	Install these on the host once:
39	
40	| Package          | Notes                                                |
41	|------------------|------------------------------------------------------|
42	| `git`            | clone the repo and its submodules                    |
43	| C/C++ toolchain  | clang or gcc; needed by QEMU and the plugin          |
44	| `cmake` >= 3.20  | vsim build                                           |
45	| `ninja`          | vsim default generator                               |
46	| `python3`        | plugin tests, demo scripts                           |
47	| `glib-2.0` dev   | QEMU plugin link line                                |
48	| `pkg-config`     | QEMU configure                                       |
49	| `podman`         | runs vsim builds inside `vsim-env:latest` container  |
50	| Verilator        | auto-detected; set `VSIM_VERILATOR_EXECUTABLE` if needed |
51	| QEMU's own deps  | pixman, slirp, ... see `QEMU/README.rst`      |
52	| RISC-V toolchain | `riscv64-unknown-elf-{gcc,nm,objdump}` (Andes v5d)   |
53	
54	The Andes RISC-V toolchain is needed to build the fixtures and to
55	resolve symbols for PC-mode. The harness scripts default to
56	`/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast540/.../bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm`;
57	override with `NM=/your/path/to/nm` if you keep it elsewhere.
58	
59	### 1.2 Clone with submodules
60	
61	```sh
62	git clone --recursive https://gitea.andestech.com/nick/hybrid_sim
63	cd hybrid_sim
64	```
65	
66	If you forgot `--recursive`:
67	
68	```sh
69	git submodule update --init --recursive
70	```
71	
72	Submodules under this repo:
73	
74	| Path             | What it is                                          |
75	|------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
76	| `QEMU/`   | QEMU 9.x fork that hosts the TCG plugin (branch: `hybrid`) |
77	| `verilator/`   | vsim sources (CMake + SystemC + Verilator)          |
78	| `tools/simpoint/`| SimPoint 3.2 clustering binary (UCSD)               |
79	
80	### 1.3 Per-host config (`config.env`)
81	
82	The repo ships a template `config.env.example` listing per-host paths
83	that cannot live in the build system (notably the Andes RISC-V
84	toolchain root, which `setup.sh` does NOT build).
85	
86	On the first `source ./setup.sh`, the template is copied to
87	`./config.env` (gitignored) so your edits never touch git history. If
88	the toolchain lives somewhere other than the default, edit
89	`config.env`:
90	
91	```sh
92	# config.env
93	HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast540/build-toolchain/linux/nds64le-elf-newlib-v5d
94	```
95	
96	The single variable today is:
97	
98	| Variable          | What it points at                                                  |
99	|-------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|
100	| `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN`| Toolchain root. `$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/` must contain `riscv64-unknown-elf-{gcc,ld,nm,objdump,...}`. |
101	
102	How it propagates:
103	
104	- `setup.sh` sources `config.env`, validates `$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/`
105	  exists, and `export`s the variable so all child processes see it.
106	- The fixture `Makefile` (`tests/fixtures/Makefile`) defaults
107	  `TOOLCHAIN` to `$(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)` and aborts with a clear error if

212	## 2. Configuring the simulator
213	
214	There are four configuration surfaces. Most users only touch the env
215	vars in 2.1.
216	
217	### 2.1 Environment variables (the only ones you usually set)
218	
219	`setup.sh` exports these for you. Override only if your artifacts live
220	somewhere non-default.
221	
222	| Variable        | Default                                          | Used by                  |
223	|-----------------|--------------------------------------------------|--------------------------|
224	| `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN` | From `config.env` (sec 1.3); toolchain root  | Makefile, NM derivation  |
225	| `VSIM_QEMU`     | `build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64`                 | every harness            |
226	| `VSIM_PLUGIN`   | `qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so`               | every harness            |
227	| `VSIM_BIN`      | first `verilator/build/sim_*`                  | every harness            |
228	| `VSIM_ELF`      | `tests/fixtures/$FIXTURE.elf`           | harness scripts          |
229	| `SIMPOINT_BIN`  | `tools/simpoint/bin/simpoint`                    | M4 demos              |
230	| `NM`            | `$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm`   | PC-mode symbol resolve   |
231	| `TIMEOUT`       | 60 s (some demos use 120)                        | per-leg `timeout` cap    |
232	| `FIXTURE`       | `rt_shared_mem`                                  | which `.elf` to load     |
233	| `TRIGGER_MODE`  | `csr`                                            | `csr` or `pc`            |
234	| `JOBS`          | auto-cap on this 128-core host: set to 8         | parallel test runner     |
235	
236	Example: override the QEMU binary for one run:
237	
238	```sh
239	VSIM_QEMU=/opt/qemu-9.0/qemu-system-riscv64 \
240	  bash tests/demos/demo_csr_oneshot.sh
241	```
242	
243	### 2.2 The vsim CPU configuration YAML
244	
245	`verilator/config.yaml` selects which Andes core to verilate. The
246	default is `ax45mpv_premium`:
247	
248	```yaml
249	cpus:
250	  ax45mpv_premium:
251	    cpu_series: 45
252	    rtl_package: ax45mpv_premium
253	    cpp_wrapper: ax45mpv_premium_cpu_cluster_subsystem
254	    config: data/configs/ax45mpv_premium.cfg
255	    config_dir: andes_ip/kv_core/top/hdl
256	    config_inc_filter: grep '^`define NDS_'
257	    extra_verilator_flags: --threads 8 --unroll-count 256
258	```
259	
260	Switch CPU by pointing CMake at a different YAML:
261	
262	```sh
263	cd verilator
264	cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DVSIM_CONFIG_FILE=my_other_cpu.yaml
265	cmake --build build -j
266	```
267	
268	`-DVSIM_ENABLE_HYBRID=ON` registers the e2e fixtures with CTest;
269	`-DVSIM_NO_VERILATOR=ON` skips Verilator (use a prebuilt model).
270	
271	### 2.3 QEMU plugin args
272	
273	The plugin reads `arg=value` tokens after `-plugin <path>,`. They
274	select WHICH switching mode QEMU1 runs in:
275	
276	| Plugin arg           | Effect                                                                 |
277	|----------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
278	| `outfile=PATH`       | REQUIRED. Drained `hybrid_state_v1` is written here.                   |
279	| `enter_pc=0xADDR`    | M2: drain when PC == ADDR. Bypasses the CSR-insn matcher.              |
280	| `icount=N`           | M3: drain on the N-th retired insn (per vcpu).                         |
281	| `bbv_out=PATH`       | M4: emit one SimPoint BBV row per `slice=N` insns into PATH.           |
282	| `slice=N`            | Insns per slice (used by M4 and M5). Must be > 0.                      |
283	| `slice_at=K`         | M5: drain at the end of the K-th slice. Requires `slice=N`.            |
284	| `drain_at_exit=1`    | F14: drain when QEMU exits naturally; overrides `minstret` with a plugin-side per-insn counter. |
285	
286	If no mode arg is given, the default is CSR-insn match (M1): the
287	plugin matches `csrwi 0x7C0, 0` at retire.
288	
289	Example invocation (CSR mode, just the minimal arg):
290	
291	```
292	-plugin libhybrid_handoff.so,outfile=/tmp/state.bin
293	```
294	
295	Example (icount mode):
296	
297	```
298	-plugin libhybrid_handoff.so,outfile=/tmp/state.bin,icount=10000
299	```
300	
301	### 2.4 vsim CLI flags
302	
303	`sim_ax45mpv_premium <elf> [flags]`. The hybrid-relevant subset:
304	
305	| Flag                          | Purpose                                                  |
306	|-------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
307	| `--resume-from-qemu FILE`     | Read drained state, restore into hart, run from PC.     |
308	| `--handoff-out FILE`          | Drain back into FILE when the exit trigger fires.       |
309	| `--shared-mem-path FILE`      | mmap FILE as RAM (zero-copy share with QEMU).           |
310	| `--shared-mem-size BYTES`     | Size of the shared region. Match QEMU `-m`.             |
311	| `--shared-mem-base HEX`       | Guest physical address where file offset 0 lands.       |
312	| `--hybrid-exit-pc 0xADDR`     | M2 exit: drain when this PC retires.                    |
313	| `--hybrid-icount N`           | M3 exit: drain after N committed insns (vsim side).     |
314	| `--jtag-port N`               | Open the JTAG bitbang port (e.g. OpenOCD).              |
315	| `--log-level N`               | 0=trace .. 5=critical .. 6=off (default 2=info)         |
316	
317	Defaults for `--shared-mem-base` is `0x80000000` (the QEMU `virt` /
318	`andes_ae350` RAM base). Most users never override it.
319	
320	Run `$VSIM_BIN --help` for the full list (waveform/save/restore are
321	license-gated and off by default).
322	
323	The shared mmaps created by the shell harnesses (`tests/e2e.sh`,
324	`tests/demos/*.sh`, `tests/plugin/*.sh`) are hardcoded 128 MiB sparse
325	files under `/dev/shm` (`mktemp -p /dev/shm`).
326

328	
329	## 3. Switching modes - which trigger to use
330	
331	| ID  | Trigger                                | Where        | When to pick it                                                |
332	|-----|----------------------------------------|--------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|
333	| M1  | `csrwi 0x7C0, 0/1` insn match          | QEMU1 + vsim | Default. Your binary can embed `csrwi` markers.                |
334	| M2  | PC equals `_hybrid_{enter,exit}_pc`    | QEMU1 + vsim | Binary is yours, but you cannot insert CSR markers.            |
335	| M3  | Retired-instruction count              | QEMU1 + vsim | Binary is NOT yours (no CSR/symbol). Use a spin loop / blob.   |
336	| M4  | BBV emit + offline SimPoint cluster    | QEMU1 only   | Phase identification before the real run.                      |
337	| M5  | Drain at end of slice K                | QEMU1        | Replay one cluster representative slice on vsim.               |
338	
339	M1/M2/M3 are the three ways to delimit the ROI. M4/M5 stack on top
340	of them for SimPoint-style phase replay. Every run ends at vsim's
341	exit-trigger drain.
342	
343	Decision flow:
344	
345	```
346	Can you edit the binary?
347	  yes -> insert csrwi 0x7C0, 0/1 around the ROI -> M1
348	  no  -> Does it export _hybrid_enter_pc / _hybrid_exit_pc?
349	           yes -> M2
350	           no  -> Use icount  -> M3
351	You want phase-aware replay?  -> M4 + M5
352	```
353	
354	> **Writing a kernel for cycle measurement (M1/M2):** keep the measured
355	> kernel anchored inside the `csrwi 0x7C0,0/1` span -- read its inputs and
356	> write its outputs through memory inside the span, or wrap the kernel in a
357	> `__attribute__((noinline))` function called between the markers. The
358	> markers' `"memory"` clobber pins memory I/O but not register-only compute,
359	> so a kernel that carries live vector values in registers across the
360	> boundary may be hoisted/sunk out of the measured window. See
361	> `tests/fixtures/runtime/rt_c_helpers.h`.
362

591	| Symptom                                                | Cause / fix                                                          |
592	|--------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
593	| `skip: ... not built; run 'make' ...`                  | `source ./setup.sh` and `make -C tests/fixtures`            |
594	| `QEMU 1 expected exit 200, got 0`                      | Trigger never fired. Wrong mode / wrong PC / wrong icount value.     |

596	| `missing _hybrid_enter_pc/_hybrid_exit_pc symbols`     | M2 needs a fixture with those labels. Rebuild or use M1.             |
597	| `vsim drained pc=0x... not in icount_spin loop`        | `VSIM_ICOUNT` too small / wrong fixture for M3.                      |
598	| Whole suite times out under `scripts/run_e2e.sh`               | Set `JOBS=8`. Default 128 saturates a 128-core host.                 |
599	| `[FAIL] [N/M] ... -> /tmp/e2e-XXXX/...log`             | Open that log; it is the full stdout+stderr of the failing leg.      |

1	# Switching-Mode Tutorial and Exercises
2	
3	Status: draft for review
4	Audience: engineer running the hybrid co-simulator for the first time
5	Scope: every switching mode (M1-M5) the repo ships, with copy-paste
6	commands and one exercise per mode.
7	
8	---
9	
10	## 0. What "switching mode" means
11	
12	The hybrid simulator runs a program across two phases:
13	
14	```
15	   QEMU1  --(state file + shared mmap)-->  vsim
16	   (fast)                                 (cycle accurate; run ends here)
17	```
18	
19	A "switching mode" is the RULE that decides WHEN each leg drains its
20	state and hands off. The codebase ships five rules (M1-M5). They
21	plug into the same harness; you pick the rule with plugin args and
22	vsim CLI flags. The fixture binary does NOT need to change between
23	rules (one fixture can be driven by several modes). Every run ends at
24	vsim's exit-trigger drain; there is no QEMU2 leg.
25	
26	This document teaches one mode at a time, then exercises that
27	combine modes.
28	
29	### Quick map
30	
31	| ID | Name                           | Drain trigger                                   | Used at        |
32	|----|--------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------|----------------|
33	| M1 | CSR insn match (default)       | `csrwi 0x7C0, 0` (enter) / `csrwi 0x7C0, 1` (exit) | QEMU1, vsim    |
34	| M2 | PC symbol resolve              | PC equals `_hybrid_enter_pc` / `_hybrid_exit_pc`   | QEMU1, vsim    |
35	| M3 | icount                         | N retired instructions                          | QEMU1, vsim    |
36	| M4 | BBV profile + SimPoint cluster | Plugin emits 1 row per slice; offline clustering | QEMU1 + tool   |
37	| M5 | slice-consume                  | End of slice index K                             | QEMU1          |
38	
39	M1/M2/M3 are entry/exit triggers (the "boundary" question).
40	M4/M5 are pipeline stages for the SimPoint flow.
41	The vsim exit-trigger drain is the natural end-of-run signal.
42	
43	---
44	
45	## 1. One-time prerequisites
46	
47	Build everything once. Each command is idempotent.
48	
49	```sh
50	cd /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim
51	source ./setup.sh         # qemu + vsim + plugin + simpoint
52	```
53	
54	You should now have:
55	
56	| Artifact                                  | Purpose                           |
57	|-------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------|
58	| `build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64`          | QEMU binary (phase 1)             |
59	| `verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium`   | vsim binary (phase 2)             |
60	| `qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so`        | TCG plugin (state drainer)        |
61	| `tools/simpoint/bin/simpoint`             | SimPoint clustering tool (M4)     |

75	## 2. M1 - CSR insn match (the default path)
76	
77	### What it does
78	
79	QEMU1's plugin pattern-matches the encoding `csrwi 0x7C0, 0` at retire
80	time. On hit it drains state to `outfile` and exits 200. vsim does the
81	same on `csrwi 0x7C0, 1`. CSR 0x7C0 is a benign vendor write on Andes
82	ax45mp, so the fixture binary embeds these two `csrwi` instructions
83	at the ROI boundaries. vsim's exit drain (exit 200 + a non-empty
84	drained state file) is the end of the run.
85	
86	### Inputs
87	
88	- Fixture ELF with `csrwi 0x7C0, 0` and `csrwi 0x7C0, 1` in its source.
89	  Every C-level fixture (rt_c_v_regs, rt_c_matmul, etc.) has these.
90	
91	### Output
92	
93	- Phase-by-phase log line + final `exit 0`.
94	
95	### Run it
96	
97	```sh
98	cd /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim
99	bash tests/demos/demo_csr_oneshot.sh
100	```
101	
102	Expected last line:
103	
104	```
105	[demo M1] PASS (CSR insn match (M1))
106	```
107	
108	### Drill-down (what the demo does internally)
109	
110	Inside, the demo calls the generic harness:
111	
112	```sh
113	FIXTURE=rt_c_v_regs TRIGGER_MODE=csr \
114	  bash tests/e2e.sh
115	```
116	
117	The plugin gets `outfile=<state.bin>` and nothing else - that is the
118	M1 default. vsim is launched without `--hybrid-exit-pc` and without
119	`--hybrid-icount`, so its ELF pre-scanner watches for `csrwi 0x7C0, 1`
120	PCs at retire.

138	## 3. M2 - PC symbol resolve
139	
140	### What it does
141	
142	Same handoff as M1 but the trigger is a PC value (not an opcode
143	match). The harness runs `nm` on the ELF to resolve symbols
144	`_hybrid_enter_pc` and `_hybrid_exit_pc`, then passes:
145	
146	- `enter_pc=0x<addr>` to the QEMU plugin (QEMU1 drains there)
147	- `--hybrid-exit-pc 0x<addr>` to vsim (vsim drains there)
148	
149	CSR-mode matchers are bypassed; the `csrwi 0x7C0, *` instructions in
150	the binary become inert (CSR 0x7C0 is a benign vendor-defined write).
151	
152	This proves you can hand off WITHOUT modifying the source.
153	
154	### Inputs
155	
156	- Same fixture as M1 (`rt_c_v_regs`), but the ELF must define
157	  `_hybrid_enter_pc` and `_hybrid_exit_pc` symbols. The C-level
158	  fixtures all do.
159	
160	### Output
161	
162	- `exit 0`, last log line `[demo M2] PASS`.
163	
164	### Run it
165	
166	```sh
167	bash tests/demos/demo_pc_oneshot.sh
168	```

170	### Drill-down

172	```sh
173	ENTER_PC=$(riscv64-unknown-elf-nm --defined-only \
174	              tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_regs.elf | \
175	              awk '$3=="_hybrid_enter_pc"{print $1}')
176	EXIT_PC=$(riscv64-unknown-elf-nm --defined-only \
177	              tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_regs.elf | \
178	              awk '$3=="_hybrid_exit_pc"{print $1}')
179	
180	# QEMU plugin arg
181	... -plugin libhybrid_handoff.so,outfile=$STATE,enter_pc=0x$ENTER_PC
182	
183	# vsim arg
184	... --hybrid-exit-pc 0x$EXIT_PC
185	```

204	## 4. M3 - icount round-trip
205	
206	### What it does
207	
208	Both legs drain on retired-instruction count alone. No CSR, no PC
209	symbol. Suitable for CSR-less workloads (an infinite spin loop, a
210	benchmark you cannot edit, etc.).
211	
212	- QEMU plugin: `icount=N1` -> drain at the N1-th retired insn
213	- vsim: `--hybrid-icount N2` -> drain N2 insns after resume
214	
215	### Inputs
216	
217	- Any ELF; `icount_spin.elf` is the canonical CSR-less fixture.
218	
219	### Output
220	
221	- Both QEMU1 and vsim exit 200 with a non-empty state file
222	  (`icount_spin` spins forever, so the icount drain is the only way
223	  the run can end).

248	## 5. M4 - BBV profile + SimPoint cluster
249	
250	### What it does
251	
252	QEMU plugin emits one Basic-Block-Vector (BBV) row per slice of N
253	retired insns. The output is a SimPoint `.bb` file. Offline,
254	`tools/simpoint/bin/simpoint` reads it and clusters the rows into K
255	representative phases.
256	
257	This is the SimPoint "profile" pass. It produces:
258	
259	- `simpts` file: 1 line per cluster, `<slice_idx> <cluster_id>`
260	- `weights` file: 1 line per cluster, `<weight> <cluster_id>`
261	
262	Later, M5 replays just those representative slices.
263	
264	### Inputs
265	
266	- Any ELF. CSR-less or not - the plugin emits BBV rows regardless.
267	
268	### Output
269	
270	- `WORKDIR/<elf>.bb`, `WORKDIR/simpts`, `WORKDIR/weights` persist on
271	  disk so that M5 can consume them.
272	
273	### Run it
274	
275	```sh
276	WORKDIR=/tmp/m4-profile \
277	  bash tests/demos/demo_bbv_profile.sh
278	```
279	
280	Override the slice and total count:
281	
282	```sh
283	WORKDIR=/tmp/m4-bigger SLICE=2000 ICOUNT=20000 MAXK=4 \
284	  bash tests/demos/demo_bbv_profile.sh
285	```
286	
287	Expected rows = `ICOUNT / SLICE`. The demo asserts this.
288	
289	### Drill-down: plugin args
290	
291	```
292	-plugin libhybrid_handoff.so,\
293	        outfile=$STATE,\
294	        bbv_out=$WORKDIR/profile.bb,\
295	        slice=1000,\
296	        icount=10000
297	```
298	
299	`slice` is shared with M5; `bbv_out=` is what activates emit mode.
300

311	## 6. M5 - slice-consume entry
312	
313	### What it does
314	
315	QEMU plugin drains at the end of slice K (0-based), where each slice
316	is N retired insns. This is the SimPoint "replay" entry: you ran M4
317	once, picked phase K, and now you want vsim to start from the END of
318	slice K (the QEMU drain leaves you with exactly that architectural
319	state).
320	
321	Plugin args:
322	
323	- `slice=N` (insns per slice; SAME N as the profile pass)
324	- `slice_at=K` (drain at the end of the K-th slice, 0-based)
325	- `icount=M` (safety fallback - if K is invalid, drain at M anyway)
326	
327	### Inputs
328	
329	- Same ELF as the profile pass. Same `slice=N`.
330	- K from `simpts` (T4 output) OR from env `SLICE_AT`.
331	
332	### Output
333	
334	- State file drained at the slice boundary. PC inside the ROI.
335	
336	### Run it
337	
338	Using M4's output directly:
339	
340	```sh
341	WORKDIR=/tmp/m4-profile bash tests/demos/demo_bbv_profile.sh
342	SIMPTS=/tmp/m4-profile/simpts \
343	  bash tests/demos/demo_slice_consume_roundtrip.sh
344	```
345	
346	Manual K choice:
347	
348	```sh
349	SLICE=1000 SLICE_AT=3 \
350	  bash tests/demos/demo_slice_consume_roundtrip.sh
351	```
352	
353	Inside, the demo combines two modes: M5 for entry (QEMU side) and
354	M3 for exit (vsim side, `--hybrid-icount`). They are independent;
355	each side picks its own mode.
356

366	4. Confirm both legs exit 200.

368	This is exactly what `demo_slice_consume_roundtrip.sh` automates.

422	## 8. Switching-mode decision flow
423	
424	When you have a new workload, pick a mode like this:
425	
426	```
427	Is your binary YOURS to edit?
428	  yes -> Add csrwi 0x7C0, 0 and csrwi 0x7C0, 1 around the ROI -> M1
429	  no  -> Continue.
430	
431	Does the binary already export _hybrid_enter_pc / _hybrid_exit_pc?
432	  yes -> Use M2.
433	  no  -> Continue.
434	
435	Do you know an instruction count where the ROI is hot?
436	  yes -> Use M3.
437	  no  -> Continue.
438	
439	You want SimPoint phase-aware replay -> M4 + M5.
440	```

218	  the DM; SimPoint pinned to 17783e5 stays unmaintained.
219	- Breaks: Plugin silently produces wrong state, or fails to build,
220	  with no CI gate.
221	- Source: `.gitmodules`; no CI matrix against upstream snapshots
222	- Fix: Add `scripts/check_upstream_drift.sh` that, for each submodule,
223	  `git fetch`es the upstream remote and reports commits since the
224	  pinned SHA. Schedule a weekly CI job that runs the script and
225	  attaches the report to an auto-filed GitHub issue when non-empty.
226	- Status: not-started
227	
228	### F-T3.4 vlenb mismatch silent
229	
230	- Trigger: Fixture built with `--march=rv64gcv` for VLEN=512 (vlenb=64)
231	  runs on a vsim configured for VLEN=256 (vlenb=32) - or vice versa.
232	- Breaks: No cross-check that `vlenb_qemu == vlenb_vsim`. ResumeDriver
233	  reads only `vlenb` bytes of V-reg payload; upper bytes left as
234	  uninitialized scratch. Garbage in V regs.
235	- Source: gap in `verilator/src/hybrid/v_regfile_xfer.hpp` and ABI
236	  validator
237	- Fix: At handoff entry, before any V transport, ResumeDriver reads
238	  the hart's `vlenb` CSR (0xC22) via Abstract Command and compares
239	  against `state.vlenb`. Mismatch aborts with a clear error naming
240	  both values.
241	- Status: not-started
242	
243	### F-T3.5 Failure-injection holes
244	
245	- Trigger: Partial state drain mid-handoff; SIGKILL; disk full; mmap
246	  truncated to wrong size; corrupt magic with valid struct size.
247	- Breaks: The only remaining negative driver covers one scenario
248	  (corrupt-state-short-read; the QEMU2-spawn drivers were deleted with
249	  the handback). Subtle resource-exhaustion or race-condition paths
250	  unguarded.
251	- Source: `tests/drivers/rt_corrupt_state.sh`
252	- Fix: Add three negative drivers: `rt_fault_partial_drain.sh`
253	  (truncate state.bin to half its size mid-handoff),
254	  `rt_fault_disk_full.sh` (run on a size-capped tmpfs smaller than
255	  state size), `rt_fault_mmap_resize.sh` (truncate the shared mmap
256	  while vsim is mid-execution). Each asserts a clean diagnostic exit.
257	- Status: not-started
258	
259	### F-T3.6 Determinism across re-runs
260	
261	- Trigger: Run the same ELF twice; diff the drained state files.
262	- Breaks: No guarantee of byte-identical output. `reserved[]` bytes,
263	  CSR drain order, and FP rounding sources could vary. Any test using
264	  exact-equality assertion is flaky.
265	- Source: `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` drain order; ABI reserved
266	  bytes
267	- Fix: Add an e2e test that runs the same fixture twice and asserts
268	  `sha256sum state1.bin == sha256sum state2.bin`. Audit drain path:
269	  zero-initialise `reserved[]` explicitly in the plugin and in
270	  StateDrain; serialise CSR writes in canonical CSR-number order.
271	- Status: not-started
272	
273	### F-T3.7 Self-modifying code
274	
275	- Trigger: JIT or workload writes to .text inside ROI.
276	- Breaks: Shared mmap is live so the write is visible immediately,
277	  but QEMU1 has cached the old insn in TCG and vsim's icache starts
278	  cold. Same binary -> different trace.
279	- Source: documented out-of-scope in the retired hybrid plan;
280	  not detected
281	- Fix: At harness startup, parse the ELF for `.text` PHDRs and
282	  call `mprotect(..., PROT_READ)` on the corresponding mmap pages.
283	  Any write fault becomes a clean SIGSEGV with a diagnostic naming
284	  the offending PC. SMC stays out-of-scope but is now detected
285	  instead of silently corrupting traces.
286	- Status: not-started
